audit_findings.title: The stakes add-on appears gross of the partnership-investment tax liability
audit_findings.magnitude: $979.1 million filed deferred tax liability, equal to $14.90 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the $1,923.7 million investment carrying value but does not deduct the associated deferred tax claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The net book value of our investments was $ 1,923.7 million and $ 1,827.0 million as of December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively, including $ 1,920.6 million and $ 1,803.9 million relating to PTS as of December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission unless the liability is reflected elsewhere or shown not to be an economic cost. Deducting $979.1 million would reduce base value from $190.02 to approximately $175.12 per share and materially lower the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the investment to after-tax realizable value, identify the June 2026 partnership-investment tax liability, and rerun every scenario and the margin-of-safety threshold with the supported net amount.

audit_findings.title: PMG's recast earnings omit taxes that will recur under PAG ownership
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $12.5 million annual OE proxy, computed as $48.3 million of filed PMG 2025 net income times PAG's 25.78% filed effective tax rate; approximately $2.66 per share in the base valuation
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring federal and state taxes reduce normalized after-tax OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Because we have retrospectively recast prior periods to include PMG as if it had always been part of our consolidated reporting, those historical periods do not reflect federal and state income taxes that would have been incurred had PMG been included in our taxable consolidated group.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax-normalization error is demonstrated. As a conservative scale test, taxing all $48.3 million of PMG's reported 2025 income at PAG's effective rate reduces base value by about $2.66 per share and bull value by about $2.97 per share. Both remain below the $219.77 market price, so this finding alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain PMG monthly pre-tax income and jurisdiction-specific taxes, replace recast untaxed earnings with normalized after-tax OE, and document the resulting anchor adjustment.

audit_findings.title: PTS income may be double counted with the separate stake value
audit_findings.magnitude: $192.8 million of filed 2025 PTS equity earnings; if retained in OE, approximately $2.71 billion or $41.23 per share of base operating value is duplicated alongside the $1,923.7 million stake add-on
audit_findings.mechanism: PTS equity-method earnings would enter recurring OE while the same ownership interest is also added separately in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we recorded $192.8 million in equity earnings from our PTS investment in 2025, and during 2025, we received $98.7 million of pro rata cash distributions relating to this investment.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is not yet demonstrated because the OE worksheet was not supplied, but the stated purge of portfolio interest income does not establish removal of equity-method earnings. The possible duplication is large enough to change the valuation conclusion materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 OE calculation line by line, identify treatment of the $192.8 million equity earnings, $98.7 million distributions, and related taxes, then rerun all scenarios if any PTS return remains in OE.

audit_findings.title: PMG earnings and acquisition financing costs are on different time bases
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $6.0 million pre-tax seller-note interest shortfall computed from $151.5 million at 4.50% less the filed $0.8 million expense; financing or opportunity cost of the $363.6 million cash consideration is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Full-year PMG earnings enter anchor OE while only post-closing acquisition interest reduces that OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the outstanding principal balance of the PMG Note was $ 151.5 million, and the Company recognized interest expense of $ 0.8 million related to the PMG Note for the year then ended.
audit_findings.explanation: The seller-note timing mismatch is demonstrated, but its isolated effect is small. The record does not identify how the $363.6 million cash payment was funded or isolate its recurring cost, so total materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a full-year acquisition-financing schedule covering the amortizing seller note and the source of the cash consideration, net out costs already recorded, and rerun OE using the recurring after-tax amount.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with a post-year-end acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $669.7 million filed acquisition cash outlay, $10.5 million filed post-acquisition pre-tax income through June 2026, and $0.4 million higher filed pro-forma first-half 2026 net income; normalized OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes the acquired dealerships, while the June 2026 balance sheet and interest expense include acquisition-related capital and operations.
audit_findings.evidence: In February 2026, we acquired Lexus of Orlando and Lexus of Winter Park, both located in the Orlando metropolitan area of Central Florida.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but direction and materiality are unresolved. Adding dealership OE increases value, while recurring financing costs reduce it; the supplied partial-period and pro-forma figures do not establish normalized owner earnings or maintenance capital needs.
audit_findings.action: Build a like-for-like June 2026 perimeter using full-year dealership earnings, taxes, maintenance capital, and acquisition financing, then either add the net OE contribution or remove all related bridge and interest effects.

audit_findings.title: The U.K. motor-finance redress exposure may be an unmodeled claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Administrative costs would reduce OE, while lender offsets, indemnity demands, or a reserve would reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: However, we will be subject to significant administrative obligations in connection with the redress scheme, if implemented, and it is possible that lenders could seek to directly or indirectly offset their redress obligations under the scheme from dealers.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing describes an industry-wide program with customer compensation borne by lenders, but it provides no dealer allocation, reserve, lender demand, or recurring compliance-cost amount. The dealer exposure therefore remains forward-looking and is not presently quantifiable from the numbers supplied.
audit_findings.action: Monitor FCA implementation terms, lender correspondence, indemnity or offset claims, administrative spending, and any recorded reserve; model an after-tax OE or bridge deduction when a filed amount or supportable estimate emerges.
